findings.what_viewer_sees: The far Austrian door opens onto warm light but the camera hardly moves. The Austria map then dissolves in over it, and for 3-4 frames a see-through ghost of the near German-flag doorframe sweeps across the right third of the map. The planned rush through the door and the warm flash never show.
findings.evidence: At 15574 the corridor camera is only about 30% of the way to the door, and nearly all of the push happens in the last ~5 frames, while the map is already 80-93% opaque. The warm flash peaks (fl≈0.83 at 15578) under a 93%-opaque map. Exact-frame grabs show the doorframe ghost over Europe in 15573-15575.
findings.likely_cause: The push uses a cubic ease-in (ch4_sets.js:54 E.in) and the warm flash peaks at pushEnd (ch4_sets.js:148). But tGraz = tPushEnd - 0.32 (ch4.js:144) and the Graz map fades in over exactly 0.32 s (ch4.js:248), so the map turns opaque just as the push and flash peak.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the push finish before the dissolve. Start it earlier with an in-out ease (tPush = T('austria') - 0.05, tPushEnd = T('austria') + 0.75, E.inOut at ch4_sets.js:54). Then set tGraz = tPushEnd - 0.12 and the Graz fadeIn to 0.12, so the map dissolves out of the fully warm-white flash. Or simply cut to the map on the white.

findings.what_viewer_sees: While the camera pulls back from Austria, the yellow Graz location dot and its pulsing ring vanish in a single frame near the top of the globe. Everything around it is still easing.
findings.evidence: Exact-frame grabs: the dot and ring are present in 15666-15668 and gone in 15669, mid camera move. The Austria overlay it marks had already faded out smoothly (ovAlpha ramp ending at 522.27).
findings.likely_cause: The dot uses a hard cutoff (`t < tPull + 2.0`) with no alpha or radius ramp, unlike the overlay, which fades over tPull+0.8..tPull+2.0 (ch4.js:251).
findings.suggested_fix: Fade the dot with the overlay: `const fa = 1 - prog(t, tPull + 0.8, tPull + 2.0); if (q.visible && fa > 0) { ctx.save(); ctx.globalAlpha *= fa; F.dot(...); ctx.restore(); }`.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The 'what could push a continent?' globe (centred, big '?') dissolves in 0.2 s into the spin/tides globe, which is smaller and about 190 px further left. For 6 frames two overlapping Earths are on screen, so the globe seems to jump left and shrink with a ghost trailing it.
findings.evidence: Exact-frame grabs of 15811-15816 show both globes superimposed with the '?' fading. 15810 has only the old framing and 15817 only the new one.
findings.likely_cause: Two separate globe shots with unmatched cameras are joined by a 0.2 s crossfade. The Graz shot ends near lat 4.4, lon -23.4, alt 2.46 with no lookOffset (ch4.js:250). The spin shot starts at lat 6, lon -30, alt 3.0 with lookOffset [0.2,0] (ch4.js:264) and fadeIn 0.2 (ch4.js:262). The looks also differ (ovAlpha 0.9 and dim 0.4 versus 0.75 and 0.25).
findings.suggested_fix: Make the hand-off one continuous move. Replace the Graz shot's last camera key with { t: tSpin - tGraz, lat: 6, lon: -30, alt: 3.0 } and use drift 0. Ramp lookOffset through kcam's extra, `(lt,t)=>({lookOffset:[0.2*prog(t,tSpin-1.4,tSpin,E.inOut),0]})`, and ramp the look values to the spin values over the same window. Fade the '?' using A.bigQ's alpha argument (1 - prog(t, tSpin-0.5, tSpin)), then set fadeIn: 0 at ch4.js:262. Minimal fallback: fadeIn: 0 at ch4.js:262, a clean cut instead of a 6-frame double exposure.

findings.what_viewer_sees: As the shot pushes in on Rasmus Villumsen, the photo first creeps to the right, then in one frame lurches into a fast leftward pan. About 0.8 s later the pan brakes abruptly instead of easing out.
findings.evidence: Tracking a patch on Wegener's face gives dx +3 px/frame (16434->35), then -3 (16435->36), then -16 (16436->37), accelerating to -40. Villumsen's face: -19, -18, then -11 and -7 px/frame (16457->61). A simulation of the clamped crop predicts both kinks on these exact frames.
findings.likely_cause: The keys ask for crops outside the photo. The image is 1920x1434, narrower than 16:9, so the full-frame crop is 1920/z wide. Key 0 has x=0.42 at z=1.06, but x must be at least 0.472. Key 1 has x=0.70 at z=1.55, but x must be at most 0.681. F.kenburns hard-clamps the source rectangle (fx.js:186), so the crop is pinned to the left edge until ~547.86 and to the right edge from ~548.64, which breaks the eased move into pieces with velocity jumps. The last-photo and quote-portrait moves have the same issue, but only about 1 px/frame, which is negligible.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep every key inside the valid range: key0 x: 0.5, key1 x: 0.67 (key2 x 0.71 at z≈1.8 is already valid). More robust: in kbAt/photo(), clamp each key's x to [1/(2z), 1-1/(2z)] (and y likewise, using the crop aspect) before interpolating, so the eased path never touches the hard clamp.

findings.what_viewer_sees: About 0.3 s after '...Rasmus Villumsen.' a short low thump, like a voiced fragment (~80 ms), plays and is cut off dead, just before 'Neither of them made it back.' (This matches the README audio flag at 9:10.25.)
findings.evidence: Final mix in 10 ms bins: a -30 dB music bed, then -15.6 to -10 dB from 550.18 to 550.24, back to -34 dB at 550.25. The voice stem vo_proc.wav is silent (-80 dB) from 549.99, has a -14 dB burst at 550.19-550.24 and is fully silent by 550.29. 94% of the burst's energy is below 300 Hz. The raw TTS take audio/vo/out/seg/s064.mp3 ends mid-burst: its last 80 ms rise from -88 to -15 dB at the end of the file.
findings.likely_cause: tts.py trims each take to [first char - 60 ms, last char + 90 ms], capped at the end of the file. For s064 the alignment end reaches the end of the file, so the stray sound the TTS appended is kept, with only an 8 ms fade-out.
findings.code_location: tools/tts.py:99-102; audio/vo/out/seg/s064.mp3; VO is loaded in tools/mix.py:29-30
findings.suggested_fix: Without changing any timing, mute the voice stem from 550.10 to 550.28 s with 10 ms ramps, for example a 'vo_mutes' list applied in mix.py right after line 30. Then remix and remux; no video re-render is needed. Longer term, in tts.py:99 end each clip at the last sample above about -45 dB within the final word, not at the alignment end.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The fade to white after 'Neither of them made it back' never reaches white. The empty-ice shot dissolves in while Villumsen's face is still visible, so his face ghosts over the ice sheet for about 0.4 s as the narrator says 'They found Wegener's body'.
findings.evidence: Mean frame brightness peaks at only about 185/255 (16634-16637). Exact frames 16633-16645 show the face superimposed on the ice coast.
findings.likely_cause: The photo's white ramp `prog(t, tWhite, tWhite + 3.0, E.in)` reaches 1 only at 554.97. The ice shot starts at tIce = 554.35 (ch4.js:149) with fadeIn 0.6 (ch4.js:325), and its own white veil is already clearing with an ease-out (ch4.js:332). The two never meet at full white.
findings.suggested_fix: End the photo's white ramp at tIce, `prog(t, tWhite, tIce, E.in)` (ch4.js:318), and set the ice shot's fadeIn to 0 (ch4.js:325). The ice shot then starts from its own fully white veil, giving a clean photo -> white -> ice.

findings.what_viewer_sees: While the mirrored stripe 'page' lifts off the right half of the seafloor, the right half's yellow polarity arrows stay on top of the lifted page. They seem to float on the tilting page instead of being hidden underneath it.
findings.evidence: Exact-frame crops at 17072-17078 show the yellow arrows drawn over the page's tilted white and dark stripes.
findings.likely_cause: The page is drawn (ch4_sets.js:209-215) before the compass-arrow block (ch4_sets.js:216-230), so the floor arrows are never hidden by the page.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the arrow loop: draw the right-side arrows (sg=+1) before the page block and the left-side ones (sg=-1) after it. Alternatively, dim the right arrows by (1 - sin(PI*min(fp,1))) while the page is in the air.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The flipped stripe page eases to a stop on the left half. Then, in one frame, six bright yellow polarity arrows appear on the left half, and the left front cross-section switches from plain grey to black-and-white dikes.
findings.evidence: Frames 17094-17096 have left stripes but no arrows and a plain grey front face. Frame 17097 has all arrows and dikes at full opacity (detector pop at [0.22,0.61]). The right-side arrows had faded in over 0.6 s earlier (ch4.js:362).
findings.likely_cause: The left-side arrows and dikes only appear once the flip value reaches exactly 1 (at tMir+0.85 = 569.90), with no fade: `fp >= 1 ? [1,-1] : [1]` at ch4_sets.js:221 and `if (sg === -1 && fp < 1) continue;` at ch4_sets.js:273.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw the left arrows (sg=-1) from fp > 0 through the page's own mapping (x = -d*cos(th), y = hgt(d) + 0.92*d*sin(th)) with alpha s.arrows*fp, so they ride in on the page. For the dikes, use `fp < 0.8` and set globalAlpha = clamp((fp-0.8)/0.2) around the fill.

findings.frames: 17219 -> 17220, 17279 -> 17280 (the 17159 -> 17160 wrap is mostly hidden by low alpha)
findings.what_viewer_sees: The four white 'spreading' chevrons drift outward from the ridge, then every 2 s jump back about 85-90 px toward the ridge in a single frame.
findings.evidence: Exact-frame zoom crops: at 17219 -> 17220 and 17279 -> 17280, both upper and lower chevrons on each side jump inward. Between wraps they move only a few px per frame.
findings.likely_cause: The chevron position is a sawtooth, `x0 = sg*(0.6 + ((t*0.5) % 1)*0.5)`, that wraps at full opacity.
findings.suggested_fix: Fade each chevron at both ends of its cycle: `const ph = (t*0.5) % 1; ctx.globalAlpha = s.spreadArrows * Math.min(1, ph/0.15, (1-ph)/0.15);`. Or draw two chevrons per lane half a cycle apart, each faded by its phase.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The 'PLATE SPEED = FINGERNAIL GROWTH' title is centred on the frame, not on the fingernail panel. It sits half over the globe (covering Europe) and half over the panel's top-left corner. The panel's left edge also cuts off the heads of Africa's plate-motion arrows.
findings.evidence: Full-resolution frame 17580: the title spans about x 613-1307 while the panel border is at about x 1017. Two African arrows end exactly at the panel border.
findings.likely_cause: pillTop centres the title on W/2, but the panel covers px = W*0.53 to W (ch4.js:407). The globe is shifted only 0.24 left (ch4.js:392).
findings.suggested_fix: Centre the title on the panel: `F.pill(ctx, 'PLATE SPEED = FINGERNAIL GROWTH', (px + W)/2 + 20, 150, { anchor:'center', size:42, alpha: ta })`. Move the globe further left (lookOffset 0.24 -> 0.32 at ch4.js:392), or stop drawing the two east-Africa arrows after tNail.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On the 'WHY DO THEY POINT SOUTH?' globe, only Africa's drip arrow clearly hangs from a red tip. Cape Horn's arrow dangles off the left edge of the globe into empty space, and India's hangs at the right edge with India barely visible, so two of the three 'drips' look detached.
findings.evidence: Full-resolution frame 17900: the left arrow (x≈684, y 830-930) leaves the globe disc; the right arrow (x≈1340) starts on the edge of the globe, where only a sliver of red shows.
findings.likely_cause: The camera (lat -30..-38, lon 22..30) puts Cape Horn and India's tip about 63-65 degrees from the view centre, right on the globe's edge (ch4.js:439). The arrows are drawn straight down the screen from the projected tip (ch4.js:443).
findings.suggested_fix: Point each arrow along the surface toward the pole: `const s = g.project(la - 8, lo); angle = Math.atan2(s.y - q.y, s.x - q.x)`, pass the angle to dripArrow, and fade arrows near the edge (alpha = clamp((q.facing - 0.15)/0.3)). Or frame only Africa and India here and leave Cape Horn to the flat-map card that follows.

findings.frames: 18018-18131 (worst from 18062, when the counter reaches 3 digits)
findings.what_viewer_sees: In the closing rewind card, the million-years counter grows leftward into the cyan double-triangle rewind icon. From about 10 Mya the icon touches the first digit, and for the last 2.3 s of the chapter the '1' of '160', '179' and '180' sits on top of both triangles.
findings.evidence: Exact frames 18030 ('22', touching), 18060 ('93', overlapping), 18090 ('160') and 18120 ('179') show the collision. It is still there at 18131.
findings.likely_cause: The icon is drawn at a fixed x (bx-210 to bx-154), while the counter is right-aligned at bx-40. At size 64, three digits plus 'MYA' are about 170 px wide, so the number's left edge reaches about bx-210.
findings.suggested_fix: Left-align the counter just right of the icon, `F.counter(ctx, 0, 180, back, bx - 130, by + 26, { size: 64, align: 'left', ... })`, and start the track about 60 px later (draw it from bx+60 with width bw-60 in ch4.js:762-766). Or move the icon to bx-300+dx and widen the box at ch4.js:761, checking it does not cover the South America drip arrow.

result.intended_notes:
Intended and reading well:
- E1 envelope slide-in and E3 letter slide-in.
- Crossfades E2, E4-E5, E11-E12, E16-E17, E19-E20, E31, E34-E35 and E38-E39.
- Hard cuts on narration beats E6, E7, E18, E21, E22, E29 and E37. The ridge line's visible part finishes before the E22 cut.
- E8-E10 'UTTER, DAMNED ROT!' word slams with hit reactions. The Explorer has no T-pose or snapping; the small foot slide during the knock-back is a stylised shove.
- E13 corridor push start (but see S6-1), E23-E24 stripe reveal wipe, E26 lock flash, E27-E28 '33 YEARS TOO LATE' build.
- E30 nail panel slam-in, E32-E33 deliberate record-scratch freeze and shake, E36 stamp slam.

Detector events that are real defects: E14/E15 (S6-3) and E25 (S6-8).

Clean stretches:
- Chapter card, portrait and envelope; the fit morph; letter write-on; lecture.
- Paleo 200-to-0 scrub: fast, but designed under a 'SIMPLIFIED' label, with no reconstruction popping.
- Smoke and 1915 book. The ~1.1 s of near-black at 506.2-507.3 is the designed 'buried' beat.
- Corridor slams, spin/tides build and gauge drop, Newton typewriter.
- Greenland highlight and crash zoom (the fastest move in the segment, smooth and eased), stripe flip apart from S6-7/S6-8, camera swing to top-down, 1930->1963 counter.
- GPS arrows, fight card, stamp, and the scrub-card arrow swing.

Timing: every visual lands within about 0.3 s of the word it illustrates.

Chunk seams: I compared all eight (14849/50, 15299/300, 15749/50, 16199/200, 16649/50, 17099/100, 17549/50, 17999/18000) and none has a look change. Slightly raised differences at chunks 33, 34 and 38 are edge-only codec noise from each chunk's x264 keyframe, not visible.

Tool caveat for all reviewers: tools/grab.py (ffmpeg call at line 26) uses the default frame timing, which duplicates the first decoded frame. The first two tiles of every grab are identical, and every label after the first is one frame too high (label N shows real frame N-1; verified at the 15065/15066 cut). Adding '-fps_mode passthrough' fixes it. All frame numbers in this report come from a passthrough grabber.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The chapter-opening push into Green's title page doesn't move as one continuous push. It comes in three surges: the page lurches forward, stops dead at 6:00.97, lurches again, nearly stops at 6:01.77, then lurches a third time to the minister line.
findings.evidence: Exact-frame motion energy (mean |frame diff| at 480 px): 0.08 at 10804, rising to 15.2 at 10817 and falling to 0.39 at 10829; rising to 10.6 at 10842 and falling to 0.12 at 10853; rising to 7.6 at 10869 and falling to 0.60 at 10884; then a linear creep starts abruptly (0.83 to 2.4 at 10887). The tile 10794-10899 (every 3rd frame) shows the framing frozen on 'WILLIAM LOWTHIAN GREEN' around 10848-10860 between surges. Detector events E3 (6:00.10) and E4 (6:01.73) are the first two of these stops.
findings.likely_cause: The title-page keys K are 0.77-1.15 s apart and all move the same way (z 0.53 -> 1.0 -> 1.35 -> 1.95). keyAt eases every segment in and out (the key's own ease, or the default E.inOut), so velocity drops to zero at each intermediate key: A.green+1.15 (360.95), A.hawaii-1.2 (361.72) and A.hawaii-0.05 (362.87). The same per-segment easing causes milder stop-then-lunge moves at the Figure 1 key A.demo (6:10.24) and the page-238 key A.squeeze-0.1 (6:55.69).
findings.suggested_fix: Make it one move. Delete the A.green+1.15 and A.hawaii-1.2 keys (ch3.js:83-84) and give the A.hawaii-0.05 key ease: E.inOut, so the page pushes from z 0.53 at 360.10 to z 1.95 at 362.87 in a single ease. If a beat on the name is wanted, make it an explicit hold instead: repeat key 83's values at A.hawaii-1.2, so it reads as a deliberate hold rather than a hiccup. Change the last key's E.lin to E.inOutSine so the creep doesn't start at full speed. Longer term, add a velocity-continuous (Hermite/Catmull-Rom) mode to keyAt for multi-key pushes.

findings.what_viewer_sees: During 'cooling, shrinking...' one cyan cooling arrow is drawn straight down through the Explorer's legs, with its arrowhead at his feet, for about 3.5 s while he stands on top of the globe.
findings.evidence: In tile 11358+ (every 11th frame, cropped) and frames 11397-11402 at 640 px, the top arrow of the ring sits on the Explorer's body in every frame from about 6:19.0 until he starts rolling at 6:22.44. The other nine arrows are clear of him.
findings.likely_cause: inwardArrows is called with the default ring rotation 0.31 rad and n=10, so arrow i=7 lands at 0.31 + 7x36 deg = 269.8 deg, straight above the globe centre. That is exactly where heroLocal places the Explorer (d = top until ROLL0). The arrows are 2D canvas drawn after the 3D render, so this arrow is painted over him.
findings.suggested_fix: At ch3.js:221 pass rot: 0.31 + Math.PI / 10 (about 0.625). The ring then leaves a gap at the top, with the nearest arrows 18 deg either side of vertical, about 110-140 px from his body. Alternatively, add a skip-angle option to inwardArrows and skip any arrow within about 15 deg of atan2 from P.center to tetra.proj(P.heroW).

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'A four-cornered pyramid', with the camera pushing in on him, the Explorer rolls, stands up and starts a second roll. At the corner he then flails upside down with arms spread, head dipping into the glowing corner, and snaps upright facing the camera in one frame.
findings.evidence: Frames 11504-11511: the first roll ends and the clip restarts (he rises and lunges again). 11512-11523: a second tucked roll. 11524-11527: inverted, arms out, head down at the glowing corner sphere. 11527 to 11528: the whole body flips about 180 deg, from an upside-down back view to an upright front view. 11529 on: idle. The camera key A.pyr4+0.1 (hero 1, dist 6.4) is pushing toward him at this moment.
findings.likely_cause: The Roll clip in adventurer.glb is 1.333 s long, but it is played at speed 1.15 for ROLL1-ROLL0 = 1.70 s, which is 1.955 s of clip. Actor.update loops non-once clips (lt % dur), so the roll wraps at 383.60 s (frame 11508). The second roll is cut at clip time 0.62 s, mid-inversion, by the 0.2 s crossfade to Idle_Neutral at ROLL1. Blending the inverted pose with the upright idle flips when the weight crosses 0.5 (frame 11528). Also, at ROLL1 heroLocal switches facing from 'path' to camera+28 deg in a single frame. And the 'path' heading dPerch - posL is dominated by -posL once k approaches 1, so it points back toward the axis.
findings.suggested_fix: Play the roll exactly once over the path: hero.play(ROLL0, 'Roll', { fade: 0.12, speed: 1.333 / (ROLL1 - ROLL0), once: true }), about 0.78, so the clip ends upright at ROLL1. Then crossfade to Idle_Neutral with fade 0.25. Compute the 'path' facing from the travel direction (top.lerp(dPerch, s + 0.01) minus the current d) instead of dPerch - posL. After ROLL1, slerp hero.root.quaternion from path-facing to camera-facing over about 0.3 s rather than switching in one frame.

findings.what_viewer_sees: When the 1899 journal page 238 slaps down, a full-height strip of the previous page (237) stays visible to its left. About 0.3 s later that bright strip blinks off in a single frame against the dark desk.
findings.evidence: Frame 12349 has a cream strip of page 237, about 205 px wide and full height, at x 395-600. At 12350 the same area is dark desk (column diff 150-164 luma) while nothing else moves (detector E14 at 6:51.67). In the same frame page 238 also jumps 1.5 px sideways (see S5-10).
findings.likely_cause: ch3.js:240 stops drawing p237 at tJ1+0.45 = 411.64 s, the instant the p238 slide-in ends. But p238 is framed smaller (K2: z 0.40, cx 925) than p237's last key (K1: z 0.52, cx 1080), so p237 still sticks out on the left. It is cut off rather than covered.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep p237 under p238 until the cut to p239 by changing the condition to t < tJ2; K1 holds its last framing, so it reads as a stack of pages. Or fade it out: wrap the drawPage in ctx.save(); ctx.globalAlpha = 1 - prog(t, tJ1 + 0.4, tJ1 + 1.0); ... ctx.restore(), with the condition t < tJ1 + 1.0.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The cyan inward 'cooling' arrows crawl inward and then jump back out about 34 px in one frame. Half the ring flicks back every 0.67 s, a visible tick in all three arrow shots (6:19-6:22, 7:22-7:25, 7:36-7:39).
findings.evidence: One-frame energy spikes land exactly every 20 frames (0.51-0.62 against 0.17-0.28 around them) at 11400, 11420, 11440, 11460, at 13280-13340 and at 13700-13760. Frames 11399 to 11400 (640 px crop) show the diagonal arrows jumping outward.
findings.likely_cause: Each arrow's push is a sawtooth: s = (phase + (i%2)*0.5) % 1 and push = inOutSine(s)*34, so at the wrap it jumps from 34 px back to 0. Alpha = 0.65 + 0.35*sin(pi*s) is still 0.65 at the wrap, so the reset is fully visible.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the reset by fading each arrow at the ends of its cycle. At ch3_lib.js:92 use const a = Math.sin(Math.PI * s), or (1 - s) * Math.min(1, s * 4). Each arrow then fades out as it finishes its push and fades in as it restarts.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On the photoreal globe ('one stubborn man to make the case out loud') a quake rumble plays, but the globe and the two highlighted coasts barely move. The designed 'continents twitch apart' beat doesn't register.
findings.evidence: Over frames 14298-14315 the centroids of the South America and Africa overlays move 3 px or less, and the gap between them changes by about 2 px. Motion energy stays at 0.1-0.46 (effectively static). The rumble_quake cue at 476.53 s is audible: master RMS is about 1 dB above audio/mix_nosfx.wav during speech and 7.5 dB above it in the 477.5-478.2 s pause. The README audio flag at 7:56.65-7:57.65 falls in this window.
findings.likely_cause: The shake keys jitter lat/lon by at most ±0.45 deg, and the coast strokes split by only 0.6 deg. At alt 2.42 that is about 3-5 px on screen. The orange fill is in the overlay texture and doesn't move at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Scale the gag up so it reads. Jitter about ±3 deg, or add a 10-16 px screen shake in extra() decaying over 0.5 s. Split the coasts by about 3 deg with E.outBack and hold for about 0.4 s. If the twitch should stay subtle, drop the rumble_quake cue or lower it by about 8 dB so the sound doesn't promise an event that isn't shown.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'squeeze toward a tetrahedron', journal page 238 sits still, then lunges into a 2x zoom in about 0.7 s while the yellow outline of figure 5a draws. It then hard-cuts with a flash to page 239, so the highlighted figure is never seen at rest.
findings.evidence: Energy is 0.09 at 12471 (page static), then rises from 3 to 27 (peak at 12482, the largest non-cut motion in the segment) and is still 5.2 at 12491. The cut is at 12492. The outline draws from 415.74 to 416.24 (12472-12487), so the finished outline is on screen for only about 4 frames, while the page is still decelerating.
findings.likely_cause: K2's last segment (A.squeeze-0.1 to tJ2+0.05) packs a 2.08x zoom into 0.73 s that ends at the cut, and the fig-5a outline (gp) is timed inside that zoom.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the push about 0.8 s earlier and let it settle before the outline draws. For example: middle key at A.squeeze - 0.9 (z 0.6), push to z 1.25 by A.squeeze - 0.1, then hold the same values until tJ2. Or keep the timing and reduce the zoom to about 1.4x.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Two caption pills sit over printed text, and the text shows through their translucent backgrounds. 'FIGURE 1.' and 'N.' slide behind 'THE NORMAL FORM OF A CONTINENT' (6:06.4-6:11.2), and the body text shows through '1899: TENDING TO BECOME TETRAHEDRAL' (6:56.4-6:57.9).
findings.evidence: In cropped frames 11040 and 11115, the page heading reads through the pill as the page zooms underneath. In cropped frame 12520, 'tends to acquire a shape in' reads through the 1899 pill.
findings.likely_cause: topPill draws F.pill at y=112 with the default background rgba(8,11,18,0.72), directly over the page heading and body text.
findings.suggested_fix: Let topPill pass o.bg through (ch3.js:72) and use bg 'rgba(8,11,18,0.94)' for pills over paper. Alternatively, move them to blank areas: the Figure 1 pill to y≈H-110, and the 1899 pill below the underlined sentence.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On the detective board, each card's red pin appears at full size in empty space before the card has grown under it; this is most visible for the tetra suspect card and the '?' card. When the suspect card tilts and falls, its red X stays upright and doesn't rotate with it.
findings.evidence: 13953-13955: a full-size pin floats about 1.5 card-heights above a tiny, still-growing suspect card. 14058-14060: the same for the '?' card. Clue-card pins appear when the card is at half scale (around 13914-13915). 14049-14052: the card rotates toward 38 deg while the X stays axis-aligned.
findings.likely_cause: pin() is drawn at the card's final pin position and full radius as soon as the card's scale passes 0.01 (suspect and '?' cards) or 0.5 (clue cards), independent of the outBack scale-in. redX is drawn at (tx, ty) without the card's rotation trot.
findings.suggested_fix: Scale pins with their cards: draw the pin at (x, y - 125*sc) with r = 9*sc inside the card's transform, or start it only after the scale-in ends. Draw the X inside a ctx.rotate(trot * Math.PI / 180) around (tx, ty).

findings.what_viewer_sees: Slide-ins that should settle smoothly end with a 1-1.5 px twitch on their last frame. The 1918 kids page drops 1 px at 7:07.00, and journal page 238 shifts 1.5 px at 6:51.67.
findings.evidence: Phase correlation shows the kids page static for 3 frames, then a +1 px vertical shift at 12810 (energy spike 1.76 against 0.16). Page 238 is static for 2 frames, then shifts 1.5 px horizontally at 12350.
findings.likely_cause: E.outExpo = 1 - 2^(-10t) only reaches 0.99902 just before t=1, then returns exactly 1. Every outExpo move therefore snaps its last 0.1% of travel in one frame: 1100 px gives 1.1 px, 1500 px gives 1.5 px.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise the curve: outExpo: t => t >= 1 ? 1 : (1 - Math.pow(2, -10 * t)) / (1 - Math.pow(2, -10)). This is a shared helper, so all chapters benefit.

result.intended_notes: Intended and reading well: all hard cuts land on narration beats (E1, E5, E6, E9, E12, E16, E18, E21-E24, E30, E32). E8 is the designed 0.2 s white callback flash. E7 and E31 are ends of crossfades. E10 is the panel slide plus 3D reframe (outExpo wrapped in inOut, smooth, peak about 47 px/frame). E11 is the 5/5 stamp, E13 the page-238 slap-in, E17 the whip-pan to the antipode (continuous, small zoom bounce at the key), E19 the kids pop-in, E20 the chalk circle-to-pyramid morph. E25 is the stall 'boing' gag; the 2-frame cage fade and the cartoon hang are deliberate. E26-E29 are the board entrances, the red-X slam and the suspect-card fall. Not intended: E3/E4 are stops inside the stuttering title push (S5-1), E14 is the page-237 pop (S5-4), and E15 is the start of the rushed page-238 lunge (S5-7). Chunk seams: all nine in this segment (10800, 11250, 11700, 12150, 12600, 13050, 13500, 13950, 14400) were compared at block level (450k-1 vs 450k); no look change, only encoder-level noise. Clean stretches: the Hawaii globe; the bent-card water diorama (no flicker); the triangle flash; the checklist camera swings, including the 6:39.8-6:40.4 top-to-bottom flip, which is fast (about 200 deg/s peak) but continuous; the North America/antipode globe and dig ripple; the kids page (staggered pop-ins, nods, middle kid's spin); the frozen tetra with the '?' (calm but deliberate); the measure globe with tape, ellipse and X; the cutaway; the stall drop and push-in; the board push; the Ortelius push and coast glows; the flat-map Greenland pop and dip to white. Narration sync is within about 0.15 s everywhere I checked. Minor timing notes not raised as findings: because outExpo is wrapped in prog's default inOut, the board shot opens on an empty board for 6 frames (13882-13887) and the kids page on an empty desk for 2 frames. Also, cooling arrows overlap the tetra's bottom corner in s054/s055. Tool note: tools/grab.py duplicates the first decoded frame, so its tile labels after the first frame are one frame late. The frame numbers above come from an exact decode (ffmpeg -fps_mode passthrough; scripts in scratchpad/review6/s5tools/).

findings.frames: 19217 (slider pops in at full size); 19217-19326 slider parked at the bottom; 19326->19327 jump of 313 px; small hops at 19341 (20 px) and 19382 (10 px); after the G->H cut it is parked again 19397-19486; 19486->19487 jump of 215 px; snap at 19548
findings.what_viewer_sees: The yellow zipper slider never slides. It appears at full size in one frame, then sits at the bottom of the seam for 3.6 s while the narration says 'unzips from the bottom up'. At 10:44.23 it teleports about 300 px north. In that same frame half the zipper teeth vanish and the cyan new-ocean strip with its ridge line pops in along the whole lower seam. After the cut it parks mid-seam for another 3 s, then teleports about 215 px to the equatorial end at 10:49.57, together with the yellow 'remaining seam' dot.
findings.evidence: Yellow-pixel centroid tracked with a frame-exact decoder (1920 px coordinates): (801,780) at f19326 -> (950,505) at f19327; (869,575) at f19486 -> (928,368) at f19487. Between these frames it moves only 0.1-1.8 px per frame, which is camera drift. Tiles: every 10th frame from 19217-19327 shows the slider in the same place until 19327. Crops of 19325-19328 and 19484-19489 show the teeth and cyan strip changing in a single frame.
findings.likely_cause: drawZipper puts the slider at integer seam-pair index k, the first pair whose open value is <= 0.5 (ch5a.js:370, :390). open is a per-pair threshold on the plate-rotation gap (seamAt, ch5a.js:108). Long stretches of pairs cross 0.5 in the same frame, so k jumps by dozens of pairs at once. seamUnder's cyan quads (ch5a.js:196) and the H-scene dot (ch5a.js:423) use the same thresholds. The slider is only drawn once k > 0 (ch5a.js:391), so it appears without any scale-in.
findings.suggested_fix: Drive the zipper from a continuous, monotone front instead of the integer k. For example, zipF = mono([[M.zip+0.1,0],[M.split,0.25],[M.firstt,0.6],[M.seam,0.85],[M.snap2-0.05,1]]) and kf = zipF(t)*(n-1). Place the slider at lerp(pts[floor(kf)], pts[ceil(kf)], frac). Draw teeth only for i > kf. In seamUnder for 'satl', fill quads only for i < kf (clip the last quad by frac). Place the yellow dot from kf. Scale the slider in over about 0.2 s with E.outBack instead of popping it in at full size.

findings.what_viewer_sees: During the assembly ('Africa, India'), Madagascar, the pale island between Africa and India in the middle of the frame, disappears in one frame at 10:11.60. Gondwana is then shown without it. At 10:35.40, right after 'Cracks open', a large pale landmass pops into the Africa-India channel in one frame.
findings.evidence: Frame-exact crops: f18347 shows the island and f18348 does not. Block diff 54.5 vs a local median of 6.2. At f19062 the block diff is 78 vs a median of 1.7 at (0.66,0.50), and crops of 19060-19063 show the island appearing. Both flips happen exactly where the counter crosses 170.5 Ma. In ch5a_data.js, the Madagascar polygon (coast_TTT index 631 at 180, 630 at 179-176, 631 at 175, 632 at 174, 631 at 173, 630 at 172-171) is in EXCL for 171-180 Ma but not for 170 Ma and younger. Madagascar (coast_000 polygon 913) is not a member of any tracked plate in work_ch5a/member2.json.
findings.likely_cause: The per-Ma classifier in work_ch5a/export.py (lines 13-23, nearest-point test per Ma with no temporal coherence) wrongly tags Madagascar as part of a tracked plate for Ma >= 171. Paleo.drawBase then skips it (ch5a_paleo.js:76,82), so it toggles on and off at the integer-Ma step. The same mechanism causes smaller flips, for example the NE-Brazil sand sliver at 125.5 Ma (f19449) and a West Antarctic block at 165.5 Ma (f19094).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the Madagascar indices listed above from EXCL[171..180] so Madagascar is drawn throughout, or regenerate with export.py changed so it never excludes polygons that belong to no tracked plate. Also enforce temporal coherence: a polygon's class must not flip at a single Ma step, and any class change should be faded over +-1 Ma in drawBase.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Throughout the 40-s forward run, the untracked land moves in visible ticks a few times per second while the highlighted plates glide smoothly. This includes Antarctica, the 'keypiece' and centre of frame in 10:33-10:39, plus Madagascar, Arabia and the Asian margin. Antarctica's coastline and the Weddell Sea islands twitch about 4 px every 5-6 frames. In the slam shot, the Asian coast right beside the crumple marks twitches as well.
findings.evidence: Phase correlation on the Antarctica region in scene F gives 0 px for four frames, then (-1,+4) px at f19057, then 0 again. The outlier-block scan shows a spike at every counter tick (f19046/52/57/62/67/73/78). Amplified diff images at f19057, f19190, f19690, f19804, f19911, f20098 and f20128 show bright outlines only on base-land pieces (Antarctica, Madagascar, Arabia, Asia) at the Ma ticks, and faint outlines on the tracked plates. The crop at f19190 shows the Antarctic coast shifting 10-15 px against the smooth cyan seam strip.
findings.likely_cause: Paleo.draw renders all base land, including Antarctica (ANT[Ti] plus antX), from the coast_{round(T)} snapshot (ch5a_paleo.js:93,99). Only the four tracked plates are rotated continuously. At 2-6 Ma/s the snapshot changes every 5-15 frames, and each snapshot is an independent reconstruction, so shapes also change slightly.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw Antarctica like a tracked plate: rotate its present-day rings (coast_000 ANT[0] polygons, already loaded as antPts in ch5a.js:74) by P.rot('antarctica', T) every frame, and drop ANT/antX polygons from the base. For the remaining base land, blend the floor(T) and ceil(T) snapshots: cache both canvases and draw base(Ti0) at alpha 1-f and base(Ti0+1) at alpha f with 'lighter' compositing into a scratch canvas, so pieces glide instead of ticking. Do this for both P2 and P4.

findings.frames: 18503->18504 (detector E3); the slam itself runs 18506-18508 and the flash is at 18509
findings.what_viewer_sees: Five frames before the Gondwana lock, every coastline on the globe swells in one frame. Antarctica's jagged coast and its island clusters turn into smooth blobs, the gaps at the Antarctic Peninsula and the Weddell Sea close, and the white plate rims triple in width. Only then do the pieces slam and flash, so the lock starts with a twitch.
findings.evidence: Mean abs diff of f18504 vs f18503 is 6.73, against 0.1 before. The actual slam frames are 1.8, 2.9 and 3.4, so this is the largest change of the lock apart from the flash. A full-res side-by-side of 18503 and 18504 shows the coast inflation and the closed gaps.
findings.likely_cause: ch5a.js:242 hard-toggles shelf: t > M.gond - 0.2 ? 12 : 0. The shelf adds a 12-px fill-coloured stroke to the base land and every plate (ch5a_paleo.js:87, :125) and widens the white rim from 5.2 to 17.2 px (:124).
findings.suggested_fix: Ramp the shelf with the convergence: shelf: Math.round(12 * prog(t, M.gond - 0.2, M.gond - 0.04, E.in)). Integer steps keep the drawBase cache small. Alternatively, switch it on at t >= M.gond - 0.03, the same frame as the white flash and shake, so the flash masks it.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'Then it slams into Asia' the flash, shock rings and crumple zigzags fire, but India never touches Asia. Its northern tip and the zigzags sit in open water, 60-140 px below the Asian coast. India also does not stop at the impact: it keeps creeping north for the next 2 s.
findings.evidence: In the f20130 crop (11:11.00), a dark gulf separates India's tip and the zigzag marks from the pale Asian coast. Computed from tracks.json and the coast data, India's present-day northern tip rotated to 44 Ma is 2.66 deg (about 300 km) from the nearest base land; the gap only drops below 0.5 deg around 20 Ma. Tracking India's top edge gives about 1.5 px/frame before the flash and still about 0.55 px/frame afterwards (364 px at f20117 to 336 px at f20168).
findings.likely_cause: The slam is only a time stamp. The Tfwd key [M.slam, 44] (ch5a.js:120) does not correspond to contact for the present-day India outline, which lacks Greater India. The crumple marks are drawn at India's own tip (ch5a.js:612-618). The mono-cubic still has a slope of about -4.6 Ma/s at M.slam and continues to 38 Ma at tN+0.4, so India keeps moving after the impact.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an India-only pull that closes the measured gap exactly at M.slam: po.explode = { india: -gapDeg * prog(t, tM, M.slam, E.in) }, with center set to a point on the Asian margin just north of contactLL (negative degrees move the plate toward the centre). Anchor the crumple marks on the Asian coast. Stop the clock on impact by replacing [tN + 0.4, 38] with [M.slam + 0.25, 43.5], [tN + 0.4, 43] so India visibly halts on 'slams'.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'As they drifted apart', all the continents fly from 180 Ma to today in about 1.1 s right after the dissolve. Almost the whole break-up (145 Ma to 54 Ma) happens in about 0.3 s, so it reads as a jump rather than a drift. The next line, 'they roughly kept their orientation', then plays over a globe that has already stopped, so the orientation claim is never seen in motion.
findings.evidence: The counter reads 161, 145, 120, 86, 54, 31 at 3-frame steps (f20462-20477). Computed T falls up to 11.8 Ma per frame (about 350 Ma/s), compared with 2-6 Ma/s in the forward run. Mean frame diff stays at 8-11 per frame for about 10 frames (f20465-20474).
findings.likely_cause: TO = t => 180 * (1 - prog(t, tO + 0.1, M.apart + 0.55, E.inOut)) is a 1.41-s cubic ramp, compressed further by the 0.45-s dissolve that covers its start. The PLOOK->RLOOK morph (ch5a.js:761) and the TODAY chip follow immediately.
findings.suggested_fix: Stretch the drift through 'orientation', for example prog(t, tO + 0.35, wordAt('s080', /^orientation/i) + 0.6, E.inOutSine), which gives about 3.5 s. Move the look morph and the TODAY chip to after it. Lay the trails down behind the moving tips (trail(name, 180, TO(t))) so viewers watch the points keep their heading while they move.

findings.what_viewer_sees: At the invisible O->P scene boundary, the yellow ripple rings around Antarctica reset: the faint outer ripple vanishes and a new one starts on the ring. The whole globe also shifts and scales by about 1-2 px.
findings.evidence: Mean diff 1.21 at f20682 vs about 0.2 for its neighbours. The amplified diff shows every coastline, the limb, the dotted paths and the droplets moving, plus the ring ripples restarting. A crop tile of 20680-20683 shows the ripple discontinuity.
findings.likely_cause: Scene P restarts the ripple phase: drawRing(..., tP) at ch5a.js:776, while scene O uses M.aim - 0.05 at :766. camP is built with camK, whose time origin k0 = tP restarts withDrift's altitude breathing alt*(1+0.006*sin(0.7*lt)) (shots.js:29), so lt jumps from 7.85 to 0 and the altitude changes by about 0.4 %.
findings.suggested_fix: In scene P call drawRing(ctx, t, 1 - 0.4*sc, M.aim - 0.05). Evaluate camP with the time origin at tO, for example by prepending a key at tO equal to camO's tP state, or by calling camAt(keysRelToTO, t - tO, 0.3), so the drift and breathing phases stay continuous.

findings.frames: 19071-19135 (seam unchanged until about 19130; cyan full at 19135)
findings.what_viewer_sees: 'and new ocean starts seeping in' is heard at 10:35.71-10:37.03, but the seam does not change. The cyan new-ocean strip appears about 1.7-1.9 s later, together with Africa's highlight on the word 'Africa'.
findings.evidence: A tile every 5th frame from 19070-19155 shows no cyan until f19130-19135 (10:37.67-10:37.83). Word timings: 'ocean' at 635.91 and 'Africa' at 637.67.
findings.likely_cause: Both the seamUnder alpha and the new-ocean glow are keyed to M.afant ('Africa'): ga = prog(t, M.afant - 0.15, M.afant + 0.35) and na = env(t, M.afant - 0.1, tG, ...).
findings.suggested_fix: Start the seep on the word 'ocean': const tOcean = wordAt('s075', /^ocean/i); ga = prog(t, tOcean - 0.1, M.afant + 0.35, E.out). Start na at tOcean - 0.1 as well, and keep Africa's highlight (afHL) on 'Africa'.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In the paper textbook figure, 'and their pointy ends all sat close to' plays over a static map. The red tip markers and dashed lines to the ring arrive only on 'Antarctica', about 1.6 s after 'pointy ends'.
findings.evidence: A tile every 6th frame from 20344-20410 shows no tip markers until f20404 (11:20.13). 'pointy' is at 678.35 (f20350) and 'Antarctica.' at 680.11.
findings.likely_cause: The tips are gated on M.ant2: if (t > M.ant2 - 0.12) with a0 = M.ant2 - 0.12 + i*0.1.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the tip markers at wordAt('s079', /^pointy/i) - 0.1 and let the dashed lines grow toward the ring through 'close to Antarctica'. For example, keep the a0 stagger but base it on tPointy, and lengthen the line progress to end at M.ant2 + 0.3.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In the Explorer house gag, a thin dark shadow sliver floats at foot level and runs from his boots across the cabin wall, above the curved ground. The cabin's lower-right corner is sunk about 40 px into the globe surface while its left corner hovers at the limb.
findings.evidence: A full-res crop of f19640 (and f19620) shows the dark streak at shoe height crossing the cabin wall, and the cabin base overlapping the pale Antarctic surface. Every-14th-frame crops 19620-19774 show it throughout the shot.
findings.likely_cause: A flat ShadowMaterial floor disc at y=0 (ch5a.js:462) is seen almost edge-on by the low stage camera (y=0.22) and composited over a 2D globe whose surface curves away (ch5a.js:522). The cabin's pose CAB is fixed in stage space (ch5a.js:477-478) rather than fitted to the projected limb.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the floor (floor.visible = false) and draw a soft 2D contact-shadow ellipse at (feet.x, feet.y + 2) together with ringE. Raise the cabin (CAB.y about -0.05), or set its rz from the limb tangent at its projected base, so it sits on the curve.

result.intended_notes:
Intended and reading well:
- Hard cuts on the beat, computed from voice markers in ch5a.js:61-63: E1 (chapter start), E5, E6, E7, E9, E12, E15, E16, E18, E19 and E20.
- E2 and E13 are designed punch-in cuts (tA2 'cut in closer for they lock together'; tH on 'first'). They are close to jump cuts, but they are intended.
- E4 lock flash + thunk.
- E6 Bacon outExpo slam-in.
- E8 drip arrows + shake on 'the whole'.
- E10 cracks + shake.
- E14 snap burst. The slider vanishes under it, which is fine.
- E17 porch-light flicker on 'house' (lampOn).
- E21 slam flash, rings and shake. The animation is designed, but see S7-5 for the missing contact.
- E22 and E23 are the designed 0.3 s and 0.45 s dissolves.
- E24 scars headline and stitches.

The only detector events that are defects are E3 (S7-4) and E11 (S7-2).

Clean stretches:
- Chapter card and the RLOOK->PLOOK morph.
- Scene C keypiece lift and slam.
- Bacon insert.
- Drips scene E.
- House-gag character animation: Idle->Wave->Idle_Neutral->Idle crossfades, the 1.667 s Wave loop is seamless, the turn and the lamp, with no T-pose or snaps.
- Paper-figure lock at 11:16-11:17.3.
- Scars ending.

All six chunk starts in the segment (18450, 18900, 19350, 19800, 20250, 20700) are continuous: diffs equal their neighbours and mean signed RGB shift is under 0.2 levels. No ch2_sets-style look change was found.

The GONDWANA title is cut while still about 45 % visible at the E5 hard cut. That is acceptable.

The README audio flags (10:29.5, 11:10.2, 11:32.2) coincide with the impact_deep cues at -10/-8/-6 dB (ch5a.js:336, 624, 787). Audio is out of scope here.

Tooling caveat: tools/grab.py runs ffmpeg without -fps_mode passthrough. For some seek points ffmpeg duplicates the first decoded frame (reported dup=1, e.g. start 19485), so every later tile label is one frame late. All frame numbers in this report were checked with a passthrough decoder. Adding '-fps_mode passthrough' to grab.py fixes it.
